Definition: of Hebrew origin (H6721); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine:--Sidon.
BiblicalUsage: Sidon was the great Phoenician port on the coast, and Jesus names it with Tyre when He rebukes the towns that saw His works and did not repent. If the mighty works done in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been done in Tyre and Sidon, He says, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Tyre and Sidon will rise against unrepentant towns on the day of judgment, and I hold that seeing miracles without repenting is the worst blindness of all.
